Synopsis

When she stands, she’s like a white peony. When she sits, she’s like a tree peony. When she walks, she’s like a lily flower. And when you look her in the eyes, she’s like the Great King of Terror. Despite having the qualities to be a peerless bishoujo, because of the look of her eyes and that atmosphere of hers, she’s feared by others; such a girl is forcefully sent to another world. Being told that she would be granted a wish as a special favour, the girl made a wish────

“Make my eyes and atmosphere normal please.”

This is a story recounting the lifestyle in a parallel world of a girl who would be perfect (probably) if just her one weakpoint was overcome.

A fantasy comedy with magic, dungeons, and a hero and demon king(candidate) who she gets tangled up with. She’s cursed though.

OP here:

A few days before school starts, add all of your classes onto Google Calendar, with room numbers, and sync it with your phone. If you have android like me, it will automatically remind you 10 minutes before each class that you are expected to be at room so-and-so for Chem class. Not only does this help with first day jitters, but the notifications come in handy late in the semester when you are running around.

After you are done with your first week of school, go to the library and organize the living shit out of your coursework for the semester. Print out the syllabus and print out the course outline for every class. then use some MS Word magic to condense all of your coursework onto 2 pages. These 2 pages should then be placed into the front and back outside plastic covers that come with most good binders; This will be your planner/agenda for the year. If you can't fit everything onto two cover pages, put more outlines into nice plastic pages that you will see as soon as you open your binder. The idea is to make homework in your face and for you to cross out things on these outlines as you proceed through the semester.

Once you are legitimately organized, go to a place outside of campus wifi and spend the next 2+ hours looking for pdf's of all the textbooks you will need. If you are lucky, some other student has already uploaded the textbook onto piratebay or kickasstorrents, if not google like your life depends on it. Amazon is great for getting ISBN numbers, if you can't find a pdf by the book's name + authors + edition, just search that ISBN number and and see what you can find. More often than not, the pdf is hidden on some blog or inside a seedy .RAR file found on a foreign website. You may not feel like leafing through all these sites, but hey you are literally saving hundreds to do so. If you absolutely can't find a pdf of a textbook online, you can try seeing if your library has it. If they do, check-out that book and renew your checkout as many times as they allow you. Once you can't recheck out the book anymore, incur late fees until the end of the semester. Trust me, the late fee's will not be that high. It's way cheaper than buying the book.

Also, keep in mind that if your school does not have a copy of said text book, you can always ask the librarian to see if they could send the book over from another school. Most schools libraries are connected throughout the state you reside in.

Protip, buy an ipad with the money you saved and use that as an ebook reader.

Great tips, I'll add one more of the same vein...

Work out how many hours you intend to study for the semester (including attending classes, etc.). Work out how much every assessment is worth for the semester. Now, allocate your study hours proportional to the weight of the assessments. If you need to do better in a particular subject, weight the assessments for that subject more heavily (multiply their value by <grade needed>/<pass grade>). This way you don't end up spending 100 hours on a paper worth 2%, and only having 20 hours left to study for an exam worth 40%. Lectures can be treated as study for your exams, or simply taken off your total number of study hours before dividing them up (which is best depends on your course/institute).
